title: Market Failure: Final Assessment
description: A final assessment covering the key ideas from all three lessons. Reach the passing score to complete the course.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A company plans to spend $7 million on research to make solar panels more efficient. The company itself would gain $5 million, and other companies that copy the technology would gain $3 million. What is the social net benefit of this research, in millions of dollars? (Enter a number only.)
Choose the situation in which someone outside a transaction gains a benefit without paying for it (a positive externality).

choices.text: People walking by enjoy the flower garden a neighbor planted
A store holds a sale, so its customers save money
Noise from a construction site bothers nearby residents
You study hard and your own grades go up

questions.prompt: When you graph a market for a good with a positive externality, which statement best describes where the social-benefit curve lies and what the market does?

choices.text: It lies below the demand curve, so the market quantity exceeds the social optimum
It lies above the demand curve, so the market quantity falls short of the social optimum
It lies above the supply curve, so the market overproduces the good
It overlaps the demand curve, so the market quantity equals the social optimum

questions.prompt: A free road with no tolls is close to a public good when traffic is light, but its nature changes when it is jammed at rush hour. Which statement best describes a congested free road?

choices.text: It becomes a private good, because a fee is charged for each trip
It stays a public good, because it is still nonrival
It becomes more like a common resource: open to everyone, but rival
It becomes an excludable good, because traffic can be blocked

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example (all amounts are in hundreds of dollars): If two neighbors install a security camera on their street together, each pays 4 and each gets a value of 6. If one household installs it alone, that household pays 8, and both households get a value of 6. If no one installs it, both get 0. If each household looks only at its own gain and decides separately, which outcome is most likely?

choices.text: Both pay 4 each and install the camera together, each gaining 2
One household installs it alone, and both households end up better off
Neither installs it, which is correct since the camera costs more than it is worth
Neither pays, so no camera goes up, leaving both worse off than cooperating

questions.prompt: Fish stocks in a fishery are shrinking because of overfishing. Which measure best reduces this tragedy of the commons?

choices.text: Cap the total catch and give each boat a fixed share of it
Let everyone catch as much as they want so that boats compete with each other
Increase fish imports so that the price of fish goes down
Give boats a subsidy to cover part of their fuel costs

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: In a market with demand Qd = 200 − 4P and supply Qs = 20 + 2P (with no tax, the price is $30 and the quantity is 80), producers are charged a carbon tax of $6 per unit. How much tax revenue does the government collect, in dollars? (Enter a number only.)
In the market from q7, making one unit of the product releases 0.5 kg of greenhouse gases. By how many kilograms does the $6 carbon tax reduce emissions? (Enter a number only.)

In the market from q7, assume each unit produced causes a constant $8 of external damage. Which of the following carbon taxes (in dollars per unit) produces the largest change in social welfare (avoided external damage − loss within the market)?
The government has introduced a carbon tax. Which statement correctly describes how this policy reduces emissions?

choices.text: It sets a cap on total emissions and lets firms buy and sell the right to emit
The government requires each factory to install specific abatement equipment
It puts a price on each unit of emissions and leaves how much to cut to firms and consumers
It gives residents near factories the legal right to stop the pollution
